messages:
PagerDuty-Bot: alert: high error rate detected for hosted inference endpoint /v1/generate in region us-east-1. 5xx spike, tail timeouts, queue_backlog metric > 95th pct. alert_id=PD-3221
Jamie (Support): seeing page. customers reporting timeouts and 502/504s since ~13:00 UTC. multiple tenants affected. digging into logs now. :eyes:
Emily (SRE): I'm on it. hit the dashboard — latency p95 jumped from 120ms -> 2.3s, and 5xx rate to ~6% for that endpoint. queue_length distribution shows heavy tail, continuous_batcher.queue_depth at ~480/512 per shard.
Margo (Runtime): queue_depth limit is currently 512 per worker. looks like continuous batching backlog is building when token lengths spike. suspiciously correlated with a burst of long-context requests from a single key.
Jamie (Support): customer repro provided: repeated chat prompts with ~2k token context causing long decode times. they ran a script hitting 100rps from one client key.
Ravi (Infra): can we shunt traffic to warm pool or scale up workers? autoscaler didn't react fast enough because cpu/gpu utilization still under threshold — it's queue-bound.
Emily (SRE): immediate mitigations: 1) soft-rate-limit the offending API key 2) enable fallback route to smaller quantized model 3) increase queue_depth limit temporarily. which is quickest?
Margo (Runtime): fastest is route to fallback model via routing policy. we have on-call toggle to downgrade to redwood-small-int8. that'll reduce per-token latency. increasing queue_depth requires deploy config change (hot config yes, but needs careful memory check).
Jamie (Support): i've PM'ed the customer, asking them to pause test traffic while we mitigate. they confirmed they're doing a quick pause.
DeployBot: deploy request accepted: route_change(feature=auto-fallback,to_model=redwood-small-int8) by Margo.
Margo (Runtime): rolling traffic to fallback for that API key now. patching route rule:
```
POST /internal/routing/v1/override
{
  "api_key": "redacted",
  "route": "redwood-small-int8",
  "reason": "emergency fallback - queue saturation",
  "ttl": 1800
}
```
Margo (Runtime): routing change applied to edge in ~12s. watching.
Emily (SRE): after fallback, p95 dropped to 260ms and 5xxs to ~0.8%. queue_depth on primary still high but backlog draining. marking incident as mitigation in place. :white_check_mark:
Ravi (Infra): while fallback buys time, we should raise per-worker queue_depth from 512 -> 1024 for this shard group to avoid immediate recurrence. will validate memory pressure first.
Margo (Runtime): confirmed memory headroom on those workers ~38% free; raising queue_depth is safe short-term. I'll push hot-config change now.
Margo (Runtime): hot-config applied: continuous_batcher.max_queue_depth=1024 for shard-group us-east-1-a. note: this increases in-memory KV cache pressure; watch swap and oom logs.
Emily (SRE): after config bump, queue_depth peaked at ~740 then trended down. no new 5xx spikes.
Jamie (Support): customer confirmed they resumed at lower rate and latency looks normal for them. they're still concerned about tail-drops when someone spikes traffic.
Alex (Product): need a customer-facing postmortem and a short-term guardrail for tenant-level abusive bursts. can we add per-key burst protection?
Margo (Runtime): we already have per-key concurrency and per-route qps, but not strict queue-length caps per-key. adding that would prevent single key from monopolizing workers. it's a small feature but needs design + QA.
Emily (SRE): immediate next actions (short term): 1) add routing fallback as a runbook step for support 2) add an automated throttle if per-key queue contribution > 70% 3) tune alert to trigger earlier on queue_depth trending.
Ravi (Infra): longer term: autoscaler should consider queue_depth as a signal. I'll open infra ticket to add queue_depth -> scale up.
Jamie (Support): repro steps recorded (for eng reproduction):
```
# simple repro (do not run against prod endpoints) - simulated from staging
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
    -H "Content-Type: application/json"
    -d '{"input":"'$(python -c "print('x'*4000)")'","max_tokens":1024}' &
done
```
this produces backlog and shows 5xx / timeouts on staging when continuous batching backlog hits queue limit.
Margo (Runtime): debug logs we saw in prod: ``RejectedRequestError: queue-depth-limit exceeded (512)`` repeated in worker logs, followed by slowed responses. also some `BatcherDrainTimeout` traces when a large batch had many long-decoding sequences.
Emily (SRE): note for postmortem - alert threshold was set at 90% queue depth sustained for 5m. because the spike rose quickly it only alerted after significant tail impact. we should lower to 75% for now.
Alex (Product): action item: ops playbook, customer comms, and a small feature to enforce per-key queue caps. also include guidance in docs about long-context load testing.
Jamie (Support): closing loop: customer is back to normal, we've documented repro and mitigation in the incident ticket. will follow up with PM/eng for the feature request. thanks all. :pray:
Emily (SRE): adding follow-up tickets: INFRA-541 (autoscaler queue signal), RUNTIME-338 (per-key queue cap + routing safeguards), DOCS-112 (long-context testing guidance).
Jamie (Support): putting incident to resolved in 1746106234.
